clusters.headline_hint: Ukraine launches massive drone attack on Russia as strikes hit Moscow and Kyiv

claims.text: Authorities stated that strikes across Russia and Ukraine killed 19 people.
Regional governor Yuri Slusar said swarms of Ukrainian drones killed five people in a residential area of Russia's southern Rostov region.
Russia's defence ministry claimed it intercepted 822 drones across the country overnight.
A Russian drone and missile strike killed two people and wounded 14 at ArcelorMittal's steel plant in Kryvyi Rih.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukrainian cities were struck by more than 1,550 attack drones, nearly 1,560 guided aerial bombs, and 62 missiles over the past week.
Romania's defence ministry said a Spanish F-18 fighter jet shot down a drone that entered Romanian airspace near the borders with Ukraine and Moldova.
Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said a Wildberries warehouse in Koledino was struck in an attack, injuring three people.
Former Ukrainian Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov told CBS News that Ukraine will be able to strike inside Russia using domestically-made ballistic missiles within three to six months.
The Russian defence ministry claimed it shot down 1,478 Ukrainian drones over a 24-hour period.
Serhii Kuzan, chair of the Ukrainian Security and Cooperation Center, said Russian authorities deliberately inflate drone interception figures to exaggerate air defence effectiveness.
Consultancy firm Data Insight estimated that Wildberries lost up to 480 billion rubles worth of goods and approximately one-third of its warehouse space due to strikes.
Wildberries and Ozon together handle goods and services equivalent to about 8.5 percent of Russia's gross domestic product.

clusters.headline_hint: Kushner meets Hamas leaders in Egypt as Arab nations condemn Israel's rejection of Gaza peace plan

claims.text: U.S. negotiator Jared Kushner met with Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya in Egypt on Sunday to discuss progress on a U.S.-backed 15-point roadmap.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rejected the 15-point Gaza peace roadmap.
Foreign ministers from regional powers, including Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Jordan, Pakistan, Indonesia, Egypt, Qatar, and Turkey, issued a joint statement condemning Israel's rejection of the roadmap.
Israeli forces control approximately 60 percent of Gaza.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that Israeli forces will not retreat from any position in Gaza until Hamas is fully disarmed.
A Gaza ceasefire agreement brokered by international mediators came into effect on October 10 of last year.
More than 73,000 people in Gaza have been killed since the start of the war on October 7, 2023, according to Gaza's health ministry.
Axios reported that U.S. Board of Peace high representative Nickolay Mladenov and former British Prime Minister Tony Blair participated in the meeting with Hamas leaders in Egypt.
More than 1,250 Palestinians in Gaza have been killed by Israeli fire since the October 2025 ceasefire took effect, according to Palestinian official sources.
Hamas stated on July 30 that it would hand over its weapons to a new Palestinian governing body overseeing Gaza under the supervision of the Board of Peace.

clusters.headline_hint: Record wildfires spread across Belgium, Greece, and France, forcing mass evacuations

claims.text: A wildfire in Belgium's High Fens nature reserve expanded to consume 3,000 hectares of land by early Sunday.
Belgian Interior Minister Bernard Quintin announced that two fire fronts advancing toward Jalhay and Monschau had been brought under control.
Sweden sent two water-bombing aircraft and Sweden and the Netherlands dispatched helicopters to help Belgian crews battle the High Fens fire.
An elderly couple died outside their home in the Peristeria beach area on the Greek island of Salamis due to forest fires.
Approximately 600 residents in the Belgian municipalities of Waimes and Bütgenbach were instructed to evacuate due to shifting winds and spreading smoke.
The High Fens fire is the largest recorded wildfire in Belgium's modern history, burning more than twice the area destroyed during the country's previous record fire in 2011.
Around 100 French firefighters travelled to Spain to assist in controlling a wildfire in Aragon that destroyed roughly 16,600 hectares.
Officials in Monschau, Germany, reported that the Belgian wildfire advanced within approximately 3 kilometres of the German border.
In France, a wildfire in the Landes region burned 1,700 hectares of forest and remained out of control despite halting its spread.

clusters.headline_hint: Powerful earthquake in Indonesia leaves dozens dead and thousands displaced

claims.text: A magnitude-7.7 earthquake struck off Indonesia's Flores island, killing at least 53 people and injuring over 130 others.
A magnitude-6.9 earthquake struck northern Sumatra hours after the Flores quake, with no immediate casualties reported.
Indonesian authorities declared a state of emergency in East Nusa Tenggara province after roughly 5,000 people were evacuated.
Indonesia's National Disaster Management Agency reported that over 900 homes and hundreds of buildings were damaged alongside 341 recorded aftershocks.
Ceilings collapsed in the operating theatres and clinics at Ruteng Regional Hospital in Manggarai, forcing medical staff to treat patients in outdoor tents.
Authorities issued a tsunami warning following the Flores earthquake, which was lifted approximately three hours later after no significant sea level changes were detected.
Rescue teams cleared landslide debris to reopen access along sections of the 700-kilometre Trans-Flores Highway.

clusters.headline_hint: Political storm erupts over alleged disrespect to Vande Mataram at Congress headquarters

claims.text: Union Home Minister Amit Shah accused Congress leaders of disrespecting the National Song Vande Mataram during Independence Day celebrations at the AICC headquarters.
Amit Shah alleged that Sonia Gandhi gestured to Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge to stop the singing of Vande Mataram midway.
Congress general secretary K.C. Venugopal stated that the incident at the AICC headquarters was a communication misunderstanding and denied any intention to insult the song.
In July 2026, Parliament passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, making attempts to prevent or stop the singing of Vande Mataram a legal offence.
BJP leaders lodged formal police complaints against Sonia Gandhi in New Delhi and Karnataka over the Vande Mataram incident.
The Congress party stated that Sonia Gandhi was only asking for a chair for Mallikarjun Kharge during the event, not attempting to interrupt the song.
Congress leader Jairam Ramesh criticized Amit Shah, alleging he was using the controversy to divert attention from government failures.
A legal complaint filed in Delhi cited video footage where Rahul Gandhi is allegedly heard saying 'We are not singing Vande Mataram'.

clusters.headline_hint: Student protests intensify in Jharkhand over recruitment exam irregularities

claims.text: Protesting job aspirants burned effigies of Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in Ranchi.
Students organized under the JPSC-JSSC Reform Manch are demanding a Central Bureau of Investigation probe into alleged paper leaks and exam irregularities.
Jharkhand government officials invited the student movement leaders for a fourth round of talks on August 17 at the State Guest House in Ranchi.
Protest leaders announced plans to surround Chief Minister Hemant Soren's official residence on August 20 if their demands remain unaddressed.
Student representatives agreed to attend the August 17 talks provided their legal adviser is allowed to participate.
In his Independence Day speech, Chief Minister Hemant Soren promised an impartial investigation into recruitment exam irregularities and introduced a time-bound examination calendar.
A protester named Baha Linda shaved his head in Ranchi to symbolically perform last rites for Hemant Soren and Rahul Gandhi, calling them 'as good as dead'.

clusters.headline_hint: Opposition hits back after PM Modi's 'Dimagi Naxal' warning in Independence Day address

claims.text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi warned of 'dimagi Naxals' influencing public institutions during his 80th Independence Day address.
Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju posted on X that PM Modi's 'dimagi Naxals' remarks were not aimed at Opposition political leaders.
Senior Congress leader P. Chidambaram responded on social media by stating 'I am proud to be a dimagi Naxal!'.
Kiren Rijiju stated that 'dimagi Naxals' refers only to those supporting Maoists, rejecting the Constitution, backing separatism on Article 370, or advocating cutting off the Northeast.
Congress General Secretary Jairam Ramesh claimed that PM Modi invents terms like 'Urban Naxals' and 'Mental Naxals' to vilify critics before adopting their policies.
CPI General Secretary D. Raja criticized the Prime Minister's speech, calling it an attempt to stigmatize dissent and intimidate people asking tough questions.

clusters.headline_hint: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay condemns Karnataka forest officials over killing of three Tamil men

claims.text: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay condemned the killing of three Tamil men—Anthony Sami, John Rose Peter, and Kumar—by Karnataka Forest Department personnel.
Karnataka forest officials claimed they shot the three men in self-defence after being fired upon while confronting poachers in the Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary.
CM C. Joseph Vijay declared the Karnataka Forest Department's self-defence explanation unacceptable and demanded the formation of a high-level inquiry committee.
Former Tamil Nadu CM M.K. Stalin urged Karnataka authorities to register the shooting as a murder case and conduct a transparent judicial inquiry.
Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar announced a magisterial inquiry into the forest shooting incident.
PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss rejected the official poaching narrative, demanding a CBI investigation and Rs 1 crore compensation for each victim's family.
Protesters and victims' families blocked the Male Mahadeshwara Betta road in Hanur, demanding direct action against the forest officers involved.

clusters.headline_hint: NTA admits extensive errors in UGC-NET exam, orders re-tests for three subjects

claims.text: The National Testing Agency announced that the UGC-NET June 2026 exam will be reconducted for English, Commerce, and Sociology due to extensive errors.
An NTA inquiry committee found factual, typographical, translation, scholar name, and punctuation errors, alongside repeated questions from previous years.
The re-tests are scheduled for September 9 for English and Commerce, and September 10 for Sociology, with no additional exam fee charged to candidates.
The NTA released provisional answer keys for 84 UGC-NET subjects while withholding the answer keys for English, Commerce, and Sociology.
Sociology candidates flagged multiple spelling mistakes in scholar names, including 'Ritzer' printed as 'Putzer' and 'Parsons' printed as 'Parsow'.
English candidates alleged that 67 out of 150 questions in the June exam were identical to questions administered in 2024.
The UGC-NET re-examination marks the second major national examination cancelled by the NTA in 2026 following the scrapping of the May 3 NEET-UG exam.

clusters.headline_hint: Bangladesh conditions PM Tarique Rahman's India visit on extradition of Sheikh Hasina

claims.text: Bangladesh foreign ministry official A.K.M. Shahidul Karim stated Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will not visit India until New Delhi extradites ousted leader Sheikh Hasina.
Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal sentenced Sheikh Hasina to death in November for crimes against humanity.
In February, a court sentenced Sheikh Hasina to 10 years' imprisonment across two corruption cases involving land allocation in Dhaka.
Sheikh Hasina held an audio virtual press conference at the Foreign Correspondents' Club in Delhi on August 5, announcing plans to return to Bangladesh in December.
India's Ministry of External Affairs clarified on August 7 that the Indian government had no role in organizing and did not endorse Sheikh Hasina's press conference.
Tarique Rahman assumed office as Bangladesh's Prime Minister in February and conducted his initial foreign visits to Malaysia and China.
India's High Commissioner to Bangladesh, Dinesh Trivedi, met with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in Dhaka.
